name: enemies-r7
note: BL-17, owner 2026-11-12: the Dragon is concept B (flying). Three variations on it, one image each, because its bat wings were too like the Demon's: fin wings, plated-scale wings, swept pterosaur wings. Also: NO horns (the Demon has them), only spikes, fins and scales round the head; and the Dragon is a fairly bright green, not too bright. None installed until the owner picks.

dragon-fin.prompt: RENDERING REFERENCE: the attached COW on magenta is one of this game's animals: match its rendering (soft painterly, flat colour with gentle shading, soft thick outlines, no texture, no background). STYLE REFERENCE, the most important image: the attached farm man on magenta is an APPROVED character of this game. The new creature must look drawn by the same hand on the same day, for the same storybook: the same chunky doll proportion (a big head, large expressive eyes, a short thick body, small feet), the same soft rendering; never realistic, never anatomical, never gory. THIS IS AN ENEMY the player fights: menacing in a storybook way (a scowl, bared teeth, a glare), but still charming and readable, something a child would call a monster and not be frightened by; no blood, no wounds. VIEW, the rule for every enemy: FRONT-FACING, like the player characters: facing the viewer, the body square-ish to the viewer with a FAINT three-quarter turn, the head and the eyes turned a little toward the viewer's RIGHT, the body upright; left and right sides roughly symmetrical. SIBLINGS: the attached OGRE and ZOMBIE are approved enemies of this game: the dragon must look painted by the same hand: the same simple rounded shapes, clean flat-ish colour with gentle soft shading, soft thick outlines, a clear readable face with big angry eyes. DESIGN REFERENCE: the attached BLUE flying dragon is the approved concept for this enemy: keep its pose, its build and its drawing (hovering upright and facing the viewer, the head lowered toward the viewer, the long neck, the plated belly, the front claws drawn up to the chest and EMPTY, the hind legs dangling, the long tail hanging in an S curve) and make THREE changes. CHANGE 1, COLOUR: the dragon is GREEN: a fairly bright, fresh leaf green on the scales (clear and lively, but not neon, not lime, not yellow-green), a little darker green on the back and the spines, and a pale cream-yellow plated belly. CHANGE 2, NO HORNS: remove the two horns entirely. The head has NO horns of any kind. Instead it is framed by a crown of short pointed scale-spikes and fins: a row of spikes along the brow and the back of the skull, finned frills behind the jaw and cheeks, and the ridge of spines running on down the neck; all of them green like the body, short, and lying back along the head. CHANGE 3, THE WINGS, which must NOT be bat wings (no long finger bones with scalloped leather between them, nothing like a demon's wings): FIN WINGS, like the fins of a great sea creature or two open fans: each wing is one broad rounded SAIL, wider at the top than at the root, held open by MANY thin straight ribs that all spring from the shoulder like the sticks of a fan, with a smooth rounded outer edge that only dips slightly between the ribs; the webbing is a paler yellow-green with a darker green band along the outer edge, the ribs dark green. Small matching fins stand along the forearms and at the tail tip. It HOVERS: nothing touches the ground, and there is empty space between the tail tip and its shadow. It holds NOTHING and breathes NO fire in the picture: no flame, no smoke, no sparks, no glow spilling onto the background; every part is OPAQUE. Keep it at the game's scale: it is seen about 140 pixels wide on the board, so big plain shapes, a strong silhouette, scales suggested by a few large shapes and never drawn one by one, no fine detail. COLOUR: never pink, never magenta, never purple anywhere on it. The LAST attached image is a layout guide: a pure magenta (#FF00FF) field with a thin grid, a 1 x 1 box outlined in the middle (one board tile) and a dashed half-height box directly above it (the headroom); the reference character stands in that box with its head in the headroom. ONE FIGURE ONLY, nothing else in the picture: no building, no props on the ground, no scene. This is the game's largest creature: IGNORE the box for its size and FILL THE PICTURE, leaving only a small margin of magenta on every side; the reference character would stand no higher than its knee. Draw it hovering: the wings reach nearly from the left edge of the picture to the right edge; the tail tip a little above the bottom. A soft oval shadow on the ground directly below it, not touching it; leave every other pixel pure solid magenta: no grass, no ground, no frame, no text.
